term: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type
rationale: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type is by name a breast entity; within the multi-organ 8500/3 ceiling it is restricted to the breast subsites.
source_name: WHO Breast 5th ed terminology; invasive breast carcinoma NST is breast-specific

rationale: Invasive breast carcinoma, NOS is by name a breast entity; within the multi-organ 8500/3 ceiling it is restricted to the breast subsites.
source_name: WHO Breast classification; invasive breast carcinoma NST/NOS is breast-specific (PMC3683948)

rationale: Invasive carcinoma of the male breast is a breast entity localized to breast subsites (C50); male breast tissue is coded to C50.
source_name: American Cancer Society, breast cancer in men (invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast)

subset_sites: Overlapping lesion of major salivary glands
rationale: Salivary duct carcinoma is a primary malignancy of the salivary glands (WHO Head & Neck Tumours), arising almost exclusively in major salivary glands (esp. parotid) and minor glands; it does not occur across the code's other ceiling organs (pancreas, breast, etc.). Restricted to the salivary-gland C-codes within the ceiling.
source_name: Salivary Duct Carcinoma: Updates (Cancer Cytopathology, PMC7541685) / WHO Head & Neck 5th ed

rationale: Mammary Paget disease is an adenocarcinoma that arises within the epidermis of the nipple and areola (nipple-areolar complex), starting at the nipple and extending to the areola/central subareolar region; it is anatomically anchored to the nipple-areolar complex rather than the general breast quadrants.
source_name: Mammary Paget's Disease of the Nipple, Korean J Fam Med (PMC6669392)

rationale: Paget disease of the breast is defined by Paget cells within the epidermis of the nipple, extending to the areola; it is a disease of the nipple-areolar complex and not distributed across the general breast quadrants.
source_name: Mammary Paget's Disease of the Nipple, Korean J Fam Med (PMC6669392)

rationale: By definition Paget disease of the nipple always starts in the nipple and extends to the areola (central subareolar breast); it is restricted to the nipple-areolar complex.
source_name: Mammary Paget's Disease of the Nipple, Korean J Fam Med (PMC6669392)

rationale: Synonym for mammary Paget disease, an epidermal adenocarcinoma of the nipple/areola anchored to the nipple-areolar complex rather than the general breast quadrants.
source_name: Mammary Paget's Disease of the Nipple, Korean J Fam Med (PMC6669392)

rationale: Periductal stromal tumor is defined exclusively as a rare biphasic tumor of the breast (a WHO subtype of phyllodes tumor) arising from periductal breast stroma; unlike phyllodes tumor it is not reported in the vulva/vagina, restricting it to the breast subset of this code's ceiling.
source_name: Periductal Stromal Tumor of Breast, Korean J Pathol (PMC4284492)

rationale: Primary diffuse leptomeningeal melanocytosis is a diffuse melanocytic proliferation arising from and confined to the leptomeninges (arachnoid/pia); restricted to the meningeal codes rather than the spinal-cord/cranial-nerve codes in the ceiling.
source_name: WHO CNS5 (2021) primary leptomeningeal melanocytic tumors / Pathol Oncol Res 2023

rationale: Meningeal (leptomeningeal) melanocytosis is a diffuse neoplasm of leptomeningeal melanocytes confined to the meninges; a proper subset of the 9-code ceiling that also lists spinal cord and cranial nerves.
source_name: Cancers 2024, Primary Meningeal Melanocytic Tumors of the CNS (WHO CNS5)

rationale: Meningeal (leptomeningeal) melanocytoma is a circumscribed neoplasm arising from leptomeningeal melanocytes and is defined as a meningeal tumor; restricted to the meningeal codes, a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers 2024, Primary Meningeal Melanocytic Tumors of the CNS (WHO CNS5)

term: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young
rationale: PLNTY is reported as an exclusively supratentorial cortical/subcortical tumor (temporal lobe predominant); series show all cases supratentorial with no brain-stem (infratentorial) involvement, so it is restricted to the supratentorial cerebral subset of its ceiling (excludes brain stem C717).
source_name: Johnson et al., J Neuropathol Exp Neurol 2021 (PLNTY series) PMC8921648

term: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of young (PLNTY)
rationale: PLNTY (polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young) is an exclusively supratentorial cortical/subcortical tumor; published series report all cases supratentorial with no brain-stem involvement, restricting it to the supratentorial cerebral subset of its ceiling (excludes brain stem C717).
source_name: Johnson et al., J Neuropathol Exp Neurol 2021 (PLNTY series) PMC8921648

rationale: Diffuse astrocytoma, MYB-/MYBL1-altered primarily affects the cerebral hemispheres with less common brain-stem/diencephalic involvement; it is not reported in the cerebellum or spinal cord, restricting it to the cerebral + brain-stem subset of its ceiling.
source_name: Chen et al., Front Pediatr 2023 (WHO CNS5 pediatric-type diffuse LGG neuroimaging review) PMC10619148

rationale: MYB-altered pediatric-type diffuse low-grade glioma occurs in the cerebral hemispheres (cortical/subcortical) and occasionally brain stem, without cerebellar or spinal-cord involvement, restricting it to the cerebral + brain-stem subset of its ceiling.
source_name: Chen et al., Front Pediatr 2023 (WHO CNS5 pediatric-type diffuse LGG neuroimaging review) PMC10619148

rationale: MYBL1-altered pediatric-type diffuse low-grade glioma occurs in the cerebral hemispheres and occasionally brain stem, without cerebellar or spinal-cord involvement, restricting it to the cerebral + brain-stem subset of its ceiling.

rationale: Chordoid glioma is defined as a rare low-grade tumor that arises from the anterior wall or roof of the third ventricle; it is anatomically restricted to the third-ventricular/ventricular region, a proper subset of the code's ceiling.
source_name: Baylor Univ Med Center Proceedings (PMC3377302), Chordoid glioma of the third ventricle

rationale: By name and definition this tumor arises from the anterior wall/roof of the third ventricle (lamina terminalis ependyma) and is anatomically restricted to the third-ventricular region, a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Baylor Univ Med Center Proceedings (PMC3377302), Chordoid glioma of the third ventricle

rationale: Ganglioglioma (and its anaplastic form) is a central nervous system glioneuronal tumor of the brain and spinal cord; it does not arise in the non-CNS sites included in this code's ceiling (peritoneum C481/C482, adrenal C740/C741/C749, parathyroid C750, pituitary C751, craniopharyngeal duct C752, carotid/aortic body C754/C755, other endocrine C758/C759), so it is restricted to the CNS proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Mayo Clinic Ganglioglioma (CNS tumor of brain/spinal cord)

rationale: Central neurocytoma is defined as an intraventricular tumor; the vast majority are located entirely within the ventricles (lateral ventricle around the foramen of Monro, with third-ventricle involvement), restricting it to the ventricle within this code's ceiling.
source_name: Radiopaedia Central neurocytoma (WHO grade 2 intraventricular tumor)

rationale: WHO defines cerebellar liponeurocytoma as a neurocytic tumor of the cerebellum; the vast majority arise in the cerebellum (most often the cerebellar hemispheres), restricting it to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
source_name: Radiopaedia Cerebellar liponeurocytoma (WHO grade 2 cerebellar tumor)

rationale: Extraventricular neurocytoma is defined by its location outside the ventricular system, arising within the brain parenchyma (most frequently the cerebral hemispheres, also the cerebellum); it thus occupies a proper subset of the ceiling that excludes the ventricle (C715).
source_name: AJNR (PMC7051427) Imaging Findings of Extraventricular Neurocytoma

rationale: 'Lipomatous medulloblastoma' is a historical synonym for cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a cerebellar tumor; it is therefore restricted to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
source_name: Oncology Letters (PMC4734111) Cerebellar liponeurocytoma review (synonyms)

rationale: 'Medullocytoma' is a historical synonym for cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a cerebellar tumor; restricted to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
source_name: Oncology Letters (PMC4734111) Cerebellar liponeurocytoma review (synonyms)

rationale: 'Neurolipocytoma' is a synonym for cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a tumor of the cerebellum; restricted to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
